why.terrace: Black Wolves fan club and Ultras Midtjylland ('Hedens Drenge'); organised but small.
why.city: 1999 merger of Herning Fremad and Ikast fS; regional club for central Jutland rather than a city's soul.
why.voice: Privately owned company; no documented fan say (estimate).
why.conscience: 2023: two spectators made racist gestures at a South Korean fan in the fan zone; club apologised, no UEFA sanction found. Little visible inclusion work found.
why.ground: MCH Arena, Herning, ~12,150, modern and out of town.
why.rituals: Few traditions known beyond the club; Viborg derby.
why.stewardship: Majority owner Anders Holch Povlsen's HEARTLAND (Bestseller, based nearby in Brande) since 2023; local billionaire, single club.
why.women: Women's programme only started in 2024 (estimate: lower division).
why.intensity: Data-driven, physical, set-piece heavy and direct (estimate).

why.terrace: Bataljonen, official supporters' club since 2003, in the Store Stå section; loud and known in Norway.
why.city: Bergen's club, 'Bergens Stolthet'; the city's big team with strong public interest.
why.voice: Member association (Norwegian clubs must be member-controlled); members forced an extraordinary general meeting in 2021.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; standard community work (estimate).
why.ground: Brann Stadion, ~17,950, central Bergen, record league averages over 17,000.
why.contender: Eliteserien runners-up 2016, 2023, 2024, 4th 2025; cup 2022, final 2026; first Europa League league phase 2025.
why.rituals: Strong Bergen matchday culture known in Norway (estimate).
why.stewardship: Member club with an elected board (chair Arild Mjøs Andersen); no outside owner.
why.women: SK Brann Kvinner: Toppserien champions 2022 and 2025, cup 2022 and 2026, UWCL quarter-final 2024, Norway's highest women's attendances.
why.intensity: Front-foot, pressing side under Eirik Horneland (estimate).

why.terrace: Curva Nord ultras; small but active.
why.city: Lugano's football club, but HC Lugano ice hockey is the bigger passion in Ticino.
why.voice: Privately owned; no documented fan influence.
why.conscience: October 2024: Lugano football ultras attacked three young men wearing Ambrì scarves at Rivera; 18 arrested. Club acknowledged violent groups in the curva.
why.ground: New AIL Arena (8,093) replaced the Cornaredo from 2026-27; compact but small (estimate).
why.contender: Swiss Cup 2022; Super League runners-up 2024; cup finals 2023 and 2024.
why.stewardship: Joe Mansueto since 2021, run as a sister club of his Chicago Fire (multi-club).
why.women: FC Lugano Femminile in the Swiss top flight (estimate).
why.intensity: Attacking, mid-tempo side in recent seasons (estimate).

why.terrace: Big, loyal following ('De Hvide'); official fan club honoured with the retired No. 12.
why.city: Aarhus's main club, Denmark's second city; a 40-year title wait followed closely.
why.voice: Listed company with many small shareholders; no documented fan control (estimate).
why.ground: Playing at temporary Ceres Park Vejlby (11,500, mostly standing) while a 24,000 arena is built, due March 2027.
why.contender: Superliga champions 2025-26 (first since 1986); bronze 2020 and 2023; cup finals 2016 and 2024.
why.rituals: Known Danish traditions, white kit, 'De Hvide' (estimate).
why.stewardship: Listed AGF A/S; 2025 placement brought in local investors incl. Systematic Holding (Michael Holm, Aarhus).
why.women: Women's side in the Danish top flight (estimate).
why.intensity: Champions with 62 goals in 32 games; front-foot (estimate).

why.terrace: Small home support; no notable organised group found (estimate).
why.city: Main club of Jablonec nad Nisou (~45,000); limited pull (estimate).
why.voice: Privately owned company; no fan influence found.
why.contender: 5th in 2024-25 and 2025-26, cup finals 2018 and 2026; 3rd in 2018 and 2021; last trophy 2013.
why.stewardship: Businessman Jakub Střeštík bought the majority from Miroslav Pelta, jailed for subsidy fraud, who kept a role in the club.

why.terrace: Peluza Nord ultras (Sezione Ultra 2000, Utopia); one of Romania's biggest followings.
why.city: Oltenia's club and identity, but split with rival claimant FC U Craiova 1948.
why.voice: Owned by Mihai Rotaru; no fan control.
why.conscience: UEFA 2025: fines for pyrotechnics and throwing objects onto the pitch (v Sarajevo) and an offensive choreography; 2019 UEFA racism charge and closed doors after a referee was hit.
why.ground: Stadionul Ion Oblemenco, ~30,900, modern (2017), big crowds in the title season.
why.contender: Liga I and cup double 2025-26 (first title since 1991); Supercup 2026; 2nd in 2020.
why.stewardship: Mihai Rotaru (65%), local businessman and owner since the 2013 refoundation.

why.terrace: KPO Crew (2006) at the south end; small.
why.city: Kuopio's football club; the city also follows KalPa hockey.
why.voice: KuPS ry (members' association) holds the league place and leases it to the company; some structure, little documented fan power.
why.ground: Väre Areena (Keskuskenttä), 4,778, artificial turf; record 8,543 in 2024.
why.contender: Veikkausliiga champions 2019, 2024, 2025; cups 2021, 2022, 2024; Conference League knockout round 2025-26.
why.stewardship: Main owner Ari Lahti (Finnish investor, FA president), funding the club about a million euros a year since the 2000s.
why.women: Women's team in the Finnish top flight since joining in 2018 (estimate).

why.terrace: Sektion 12 on the B stand, called Northern Europe's biggest active stand; tifos and pyro.
why.city: Copenhagen's biggest club (1992 merger), sharing the capital area with Brøndby and others.
why.voice: Owned by listed Parken Sport & Entertainment; fan club of 20,000+ but no fan control.
why.conscience: UEFA fines (EUR 79,000) and a Sektion 12 closure for pyrotechnics; no racism sanction found; hooligan groups exist.
why.ground: Parken, 38,065, central Copenhagen, national stadium; ~29,000 average.
why.contender: Eight Superliga titles since 2011 (latest 2025) and six cups; regular in Europe.
why.rituals: Sektion 12 tifos and the derby with Brøndby, known in Scandinavia.
why.stewardship: Parken Sport & Entertainment, listed; Danish investors incl. Lars Seier Christensen's Seier Capital (2020 data).
why.women: Women's team founded 2024, promoted to the A-Liga in 2026.

why.terrace: Home support ('De Kanaries') known in Belgium; no notable organised end found (estimate).
why.city: The town's club since 1924; main identity of a small Limburg town (estimate).
why.voice: Corporate owner; no fan influence found.
why.ground: Stayen, 14,600, compact, on the same site since 1927.
why.contender: 3rd in the 2025-26 Pro League; mostly mid-to-low table before; no major honours.
why.rituals: Yellow 'Canaries' identity; little known beyond Belgium.
why.stewardship: DMM.com (Japanese company) since 2017; run largely as a European stepping stone for Japanese players.
why.women: Women's team in the Belgian Super League since the 2008 Wezemaal merger.
why.intensity: Energetic, counter-pressing side in the 2025-26 run (estimate).
